head: 4b382e5388e652308d2beca448666630ba6c332d
summary: The change corrects misleading JSON errors and preserves HTTP status internally at little maintenance cost. User-facing rate-limit diagnosis remains unresolved, and observed benefit is limited to the reported reproduction.
reasons: The fix replaces a misleading JSON error with a gh failure and preserves HTTP status on the exception. The reported reproduction demonstrates that narrower benefit; incident frequency and time saved remain unknown.

The intended users still cannot distinguish rate limiting through command output. scripts/shaka.rb prints only e.message, required_checks retains its generic message, and status.rb discards http_status when building requiredChecksUnavailable.
Scope and maintenance cost are small: one existing error path, status propagation, and focused tests, with no new dependencies or configuration. One review round produced only an exit-8 coverage nit.

Reported verification is proportionate to this reversible diagnostic change: the reproduction, 3454 passing tests, clean RuboCop, and a live missing-PR lookup. Check failures still block; reverting restores the previous diagnostics without persistent state changes.

Unexercised paths include a live rate limit, empty stdout with exit 8, and rate-limit reporting through pr, pr watch, handoff, and merge. GraphQL errors without '(HTTP nnn)' still provide no status. No instructions changed, so instruction loading and growth criteria do not establish an additional concern.
concerns: skills/shaka/lib/shaka/status.rb and skills/shaka/scripts/shaka.rb do not expose the preserved HTTP status. Together with the generic required_checks message, this leaves agents and maintainers without the rate-limit diagnosis promised by issue #656 and the packet outcome.
alternative: Carry a sanitized HTTP status through the existing command output and unavailable-check evidence, keeping raw stderr private. Preserve the current failure gates and avoid adding retries or configuration.
next_action: Revise this PR to expose the sanitized HTTP status through command output, and add one focused rate-limit check at that boundary.
